lesson_title: Gradient: The Ten Quickest Marks in Mapwork
hook_text: 1:15 or 1:150 — which slope destroys your legs? Most matrics guess wrong.
clip_script: The answer is expressed as a ratio in the form 1 to x, and its meaning is beautifully concrete: for every 1 metre you climb vertically, you travel x metres horizontally. A gradient of 1 to 5 means climbing 1 metre for every 5 metres you walk — brutally steep. A gradient of 1 to 500 means 1 metre of climb spread over half a kilometre — you would barely notice it. That leads to the interpretation rule that catches so many matrics: the larger the number after the colon, the gentler the slope. Do not let the bigger number fool you — the bigger number means your metre of climbing is diluted across more walking.
visual_style: Side-view animation of a hiker on two slopes labelled 1:15 and 1:150, exaggerated struggle on the steep one, with the ratio numbers stamping onto the screen.
pacing: Fast hook question, deliberate slow-down on the interpretation rule, quick close.
